deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the second page of a fair-copy or near-fair-copy draft of an official report (Gutachten). The report is addressed to the Königliches Universitäts-Curatorium in Göttingen by the provisional directorate of the Göttingen observatory together with Professors Riemann and Schering. Its subject is General J. J. Baeyer's proposal for a 'Mittel-Europäische Gradmessung', the Central European arc measurement that later became the Internationale Erdmessung. The page continues the sentence begun on the previous page. The Curatorium, enclosing Baeyer's memorandum 'Über die Größe und Figur der Erde' (1861) and other attachments, had asked for an expert report on the plan.

The signatories then apologise for a delay. Several of them were absent at the beginning of the university vacation, which held up both the deliberation and the drafting of the report. In the meantime several things had happened:
- the Royal Hanoverian Ministries of War and of the Interior had submitted their opinions;
- the King had expressed his general wish that Hanover accept the Prussian invitation to take part;
- the Hanoverian Foreign Ministry had sent a provisional reply to the Prussian legation.
That reply made Hanover's definitive decision conditional on receipt of the present report.

The last line begins the main report: 'Wir beehren uns nun ... daß wir'. The words 'gehorsamst zu berichten,' are struck through. The sentence continues on the next page, which announces that more detailed discussions are placed in an annex. The rescript is dated 30 July of the current year, which fits 1862, shortly after Baeyer's memorandum.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The page documents Riemann's institutional involvement in geodesy, namely the Hanoverian participation in the European arc measurement.
